Putting AI to work for India’s MSMEs: Microsoft, Samhita-Collective Good Foundation, alongside Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog bring leaders together on 20 November
articles.full_content:
Microsoft India and Samhita-CGF, alongside Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog convened to discuss the path towards AI enablement for India’s MSME sector, and the ecosystem-level support required to help them grow.
NEW DELHI, 20 November 2026: AI is revolutionising every aspect of how we work and what productivity looks like. To ensure that India’s 10 crore MSMEs remain ahead of the curve in this moment of unprecedented technological transformation, Microsoft India and Samhita-CGF convened with Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog for the AI Enablement for MSMEs Leadership Dialogue.
The convening brought together Dr. Deepak Bagla, Mission Director, Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog; and Mr. Sanjay Chadha, General Manager, Corporate, External and Legal Affairs (CELA), Microsoft India & South Asia; alongside MSME founders and ecosystem partners. They discussed the state of AI adoption among India’s MSMEs, opportunities AI can unlock in economic growth and employment generation in the sector, and what an ecosystem-wide support system for MSME AI adoption can look like.
The dialogue was part of Microsoft’s AI Enablement for MSMEs initiative, which is helping 3,000 MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh, Delhi-NCR, Karnataka and Maharashtra adopt AI workflows across business functions over a 60-day AI learning journey to become more efficient, productive and scalable.
“India’s next leap of growth depends on how we democratize AI, so that even the smallest businesses can adopt it without the barriers of expertise, time and cost. The biggest delta advantage in value creation from AI will come from our MSMEs and the self-employed. Their aim is not just to create financial unicorns but also to create social unicorns by impacting over a billion lives,” said Dr. Bagla .
At the event, Microsoft India, and Samhita-CGF, the program delivery partner, unveiled a multilingual AI chatbot available in the regional languages of the MSMEs and designed to help them continue learning and applying AI in their daily operations after the training ends. The chatbot is soon going to be scaled to support MSMEs across the country.
“India's Digital Public Infrastructure brought millions of MSMEs into the digital economy. In the age of AI, the next frontier is productivity. When small businesses adopt AI with the right skills and the trust that it is being used responsibly, their people do higher-value work, firms grow and new jobs follow. We are working with India's incubation network to help MSMEs move from AI awareness to adoption, and to make responsible AI the foundation of lasting economic mobility," said Sanjay Chadha, General Manager, Corporate, External and Legal Affairs (CELA), Microsoft India & South Asia.

MeitY Revises Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2020, For Six IT Hardware Products To Promote Domestic Manufacturing
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has revised its earlier notification dated 07 th September 2020 regarding methodology for calculation of Local Content / Domestic Value Addition (DVA) for Six IT-Hardware products under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017, with a view to promoting domestic manufacturing, strengthening indigenous capabilities and generating employment.
The revised methodology covers the following Six Products:
• Desktop PCs / All-in-One PCs (AIO-PCs)
• Computer Monitors and
• Interactive Flat Panel Displays (IFPDs).
The revised framework introduces a process-oriented, Bill of Materials (BoM)-based mechanism for computation of DVA. It recognises eligible manufacturing activities & processes undertaken in India, including mainboard/motherboard assembly through Surface Mount Technology (SMT), domestic sourcing of bare PCB, assembly, testing and packaging of memory (RAM) and storage (SSD), display assembly processes, domestic sourcing of chassis and power module, and final assembly and testing.
The revised methodology provides adequate weightage to eligible in-house Research and Development (R&D) undertaken in India to promote indigenous technology development and innovation.
Further, to encourage and promote indigenous design capability and creation of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) of such IT hardware products, additional weightage has been assigned to Indian product design and Intellectual Property Rights (IPR).
The revised methodology also provides a standardised format for DVA calculation and self-certification to ensure objectivity and transparency in DVA assessment made by the manufacturers. This would also enable objective verification of the self-declared DVA by manufacturers, wherever required.
The revised methodology shall come into effect six months from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette and shall supersede the corresponding provisions of MeitY's notification dated 07 th September 2020 for these six products.
Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma

The revised framework introduces a process-oriented, Bill of Materials (BoM)-based mechanism for computation of DVA. Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya calls for Sports Industry Leaders to ‘Make In India, Play In India, Grow With India’
articles.full_content:
‘Playground to Podium’: Dr. Mandaviya Credits PM Modi’s Leadership for India’s Sports Push ‘Private Investment Can Bring Greater Efficiency and Innovation’: Union Sports Minister
New Delhi, November 20, 2026: Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, inaugurated the 16th edition of TURF, FICCI’s (Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry) Global Summit on Business of Sports, in New Delhi on Friday.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya said, “Sports have emerged as a powerful instrument for youth development, social inclusion, economic opportunity and international cooperation.”
He said, “Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has placed sports at the centre of its nation-building agenda. Our approach is guided by a clear vision – creating opportunities for every aspiring athlete, from the playground to the podium.”
The summit is being held under the theme “Powering India’s Sports Economy: Partnerships, Innovation & Global Leadership”.
Highlighting the transformation of India's sporting ecosystem over the last 12 years, Dr. Mandaviya said, “Through initiatives such as Khelo India Mission, Fit India Movement, and Target Olympic Podium Scheme, we are expanding grassroots participation, identifying sporting talent and creating pathways towards high-performance sports.”
The Union Cabinet recently approved the new Khelo India Scheme, with an outlay of Rs 36,441 crore for the next five years, to strengthen sports infrastructure, nurture talent, and promote sports development across the country.
Highlighting India's performance, Dr. Mandaviya said, “At the Asian Games 2026, India finished fourth in the medal standings.”
He added, “Equally historic was India's performance at the Asian Para Games 2026, where our para-athletes secured a record 114 medals, our highest-ever tally at the Games.”
Speaking on the role of industry, Dr. Mandaviya said, “We recognise that the future of sports will be shaped, not only by athletes and sporting institutions, but also by a strong, competitive and innovation-driven sports industry.”
The Government has approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme, with an outlay of Rs 1,856.67 crore, to make India a global hub for sports goods manufacturing and innovation.
Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 sets out a comprehensive vision for sports development in India, while the National Sports Governance Act is ensuring accountability and transparency in sports administration.
Dr. Mandaviya outlined India’s intent to host major international sporting events. India is set to host the Commonwealth Games 2030 in Ahmedabad, while also harbouring hopes of hosting the 2036 Olympics in the same city.

Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) to be held in Mumbai on 23rd November 2026
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) is organising a “Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP)” on 23rd November 2026 in Mumbai. The conference follows the launch of the new series of all three indicators during the year 2026 and aims to familiarise data users with the methodological changes, data sources used and key improvements.
• The new series of National Accounts with base year 2022-23 was released on 27th February 2026, followed by updation in August 2026 on incorporation of updated series of IIP and Producer Price Index (PPI). The new series has improved measurement of the private corporate and unincorporated sectors through greater use of MCA data, Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE), and the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data etc. Adoption of double deflation in manufacturing sector in addition to agriculture sector, integration of Supply and Use Tables in annual estimates and use of Proportional Denton method for benchmarking and that of GST data for quarterly estimates are the other key features.
• The new CPI series with base year 2024 was released on 12th February 2026. It is based on the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2023-24 and adopts the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018. The basket has been expanded to 358 items, including 50 services, with prices collected from 1,465 rural and 1,395 urban markets across 434 towns, besides 12 online markets. Rural house rent has been included for the first time, and administrative and e-commerce data are used for items such as fuel, air fares, telecom charges and OTT services.
• The new IIP series with base year 2022-23, aligned with the base year of GDP, WPI and PPI, was released on 1st June 2026. Its coverage has been expanded to include minor and rare earth minerals, gas supply, and a new sector of water supply, sewerage and waste management. The series has an updated item basket and factory panel, a provision for factory substitution, and greater use of the Output Producer Price Index (OPPI) for deflating production reported in value terms.
The conference will bring together representatives of RBI, SEBI, economists, researchers, experts from financial institutions and the banking sector, academia, subject-matter specialists, users of official statistics and senior officials from the Central Government.
The inaugural session will feature addresses by Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Dr. Poonam Gupta, Deputy Governor, RBI; Shri Deepak Parekh, Former Chairman, HDFC and Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics). It will be followed by three technical sessions on the new series of GDP, CPI and IIP, with presentations by MoSPI and RBI and open house discussions.
